title: PortalUserProvider value object created without useMemo — context consumers re-render on every provider render
detail: Line 67-71: `const value = { user, loading, ...makeRoleHelpers(user) };` — this object is created fresh on every PortalUserProvider render. Context consumers re-render whenever the value reference changes. In practice the provider only re-renders when its own state (user, loading) changes, so this is rarely an issue, but if a parent ever re-renders the provider (e.g., a future routing change), every child that calls usePortalUser() will re-render unnecessarily. Standard React-Context performance pattern.
evidence: usePortalUser.jsx:67-71 — object literal in render body, no useMemo wrap.
recommendedFix: `const value = useMemo(() => ({ user, loading, ...makeRoleHelpers(user) }), [user, loading]);` Low priority — only matters if the provider position in the tree changes and starts re-rendering more often.

title: hasRole hardcodes 'DCFG_Admin' / 'DCFG_Manager' role names — not centralized
detail: makeRoleHelpers (line 105-117) hardcodes the literal strings 'DCFG_Admin', 'DCFG_Manager' inside isAdmin/isManager. NavPanel.jsx getPrimaryRoleLabel (line 399-405) ALSO hardcodes the same strings, plus 'DCFG_Viewer'. RoleGuard.jsx delegates to these helpers (good), but the duplication between usePortalUser and NavPanel means a future role rename would need two changes and is easy to miss. Should be a single ROLES const exported from usePortalUser.
evidence: usePortalUser.jsx:111-114 hardcoded role names; NavPanel.jsx:401-403 hardcoded same names.
recommendedFix: Add `export const ROLES = { Admin: 'DCFG_Admin', Manager: 'DCFG_Manager', Viewer: 'DCFG_Viewer' };` at the top of usePortalUser.jsx, then reference ROLES.Admin / ROLES.Manager / ROLES.Viewer in both files. Mechanical refactor, low risk, improves grep-ability.

title: Effect reads window.Microsoft.Dynamic365.Portal.User synchronously — no error path
detail: Line 32: `const raw = window.Microsoft?.Dynamic365?.Portal?.User ?? null;` — uses optional chaining so it can't throw, and falls back to setting an unauthenticated user state. Defensive code, no runtime risk. P3 polish: an explicit warn when the global is missing would help diagnose Power Pages script-load order issues.
evidence: usePortalUser.jsx:30-65 — effect reads window global, no console output.
recommendedFix: Add `if (!raw) console.warn('[usePortalUser] window.Microsoft.Dynamic365.Portal.User is null — Power Pages script may not be loaded');` inside the !isAuthenticated branch. Optional polish.

title: userName not exposed from context — LocationManager.jsx destructures it and gets undefined
detail: makeRoleHelpers (line 105-117) returns `{ hasRole, isAdmin, isManager, isViewer, userEmail }` — note userEmail is the only convenience shortcut. LocationManager.jsx:354 does `const { userEmail, userName } = usePortalUser();` and uses userName at line 1099 — but userName is undefined because makeRoleHelpers doesn't expose it. Symmetry suggests either expose `userName` here too, or make LocationManager destructure `user` and read user.name. Documented as a usePortalUser API gap rather than a LocationManager bug because adding userName here fixes the consumer cleanly without touching LocationManager.
evidence: usePortalUser.jsx:110-116 — only userEmail in the returned helpers; LocationManager.jsx:354 destructures userName (see CR-2026-04-09-0202).
recommendedFix: Add `userName: user?.name ?? null,` to the makeRoleHelpers return object (line 110-117). Then both styles of consumer work. Low risk additive change.
